purpose: Verified dispositions, not a blanket suppression list. Reopen when evidence contradicts a disposition.

findings.verification: November 24 rerun passed Garbodor but Cinderace entering the Top 100 exposed another live-data assumption. The builder cutoff test now checks the entire displayed species set against current ranks plus base-Speed matches at both 100 and 50. The format-switch boundary test uses fixed rank 1/11 fixtures instead of assuming Rillaboom always straddles the real Top 10.

November 23 nightly failed because the most popular Garbodor spread changed from 64 to 66 points. A deterministic partial/full fixture now verifies preserving a saved 64-point build, choosing a less popular complete build for new additions, and filling partial-only reports. The all-species 66-point default invariant remains checked against current data.

Balance applies secondary.self.boosts to the attacker after a damaging hit. Deterministic Aqua Step duels verify the Speed boost reverses turn-two order and winner, including Shield Dust and Covert Cloak opponents; Sheer Force suppresses the boost. Existing target-secondary/status blocker tests remain in place.

Both monthly usage parsing and stored snapshot validation require unique consecutive positive integer ranks and consistent unique normalized species identities. Regressions remove rank 2 while retaining enough rows to pass coverage thresholds, and reject duplicate ranks, normalized-name collisions, and malformed ranked rows. New-month parse failures still refuse silent fallback.

November 21 nightly failed solely because the live Baxcalibur weighted mean crossed 1. The real-usage test now checks evaluability; deterministic rolls at identical 75% OHKO probability on both sides of mean 1 verify the tier and badge exactly. Daily usage is no longer expected to preserve a numeric mean or classification.

Balance tracks move actions and disables First Impression after the first action, including misses and flinches. Independently verified sim/battle-actions.ts increments activeMoveActions at runMove entry before failure checks. It is excluded from repeatable core attacks. Seeded Golisopod duels cover ordinary and opening-flinch cases with only one First Impression attempt.

Validator requires unique consecutive integer ranks starting at one for each reported category. Regressions remove interior rows from all five categories, while a shorter consecutive spread list remains accepted.

The picker offers only moves with Champions engine metadata and a regression checks that every offered move survives sanitization. Rotom Thunder Shock remains in the source learnset, but is not offered while the engine cannot model it. This does not claim independent verification of in-game legality.
findings.reopenWhen: A reported common move is unmodelable, an offered move cannot be saved/evaluated, or new primary game/engine evidence changes availability.

findings.verification: The November 20 nightly collected all data but three UI tests assumed the old one-opponent, no-Mega starter. Tests now select Kingambit explicitly and scope item activation separately from Mega toggles. Uniform-list expectations include the added opponent and our Mega Stone. These were test setup failures, not a downloader outage.

build_roster.py rejects every cached/downloaded CSV unless all pokemon cells match the source record showdownName. Derived Mega/cosmetic forms still share that record's usage. Regression includes the complete captured Furfrou Singles CSV substituted for Gogoat, mixed identities, and valid shared forms.
tests/test_refresh_safety.py rejects newer-month transport errors and incomplete tables. Only an explicitly unpublished format pair can fall back; discovery records retain that fact.

scripts/validate_site_data.py checks declared/prior formats and nonempty categories with source identity. tests/test_refresh_safety.py reproduces Gogoat Singles removal and Furfrou Doubles empty spreads.
scripts/move_effect_projection.cjs preserves callback status choices, retaining upstream chance. Node exporter and deterministic Balance tests cover all three statuses and blockers.

Upstream Showdown data/moves.ts uses 50 + 50 * side.totalFainted; the current Champions mod does not override it. The pinned calc does not scale it, so battle.js supplies that power. Existing tests detect damage/double-scaling regressions. This is source-based verification, not an independently measured in-game fixture.
findings.reopenWhen: Official Champions patch changes this rule, upstream callback/mod changes, or a newer engine scales it differently. Lack of an empirical game fixture alone is a watch item, not a fresh defect.

findings.verification: Reported moves/items/spreads are top lists, not exhaustive sets. Rows can leave the list while remaining legal. Slurpuff duplicate item rows were observed upstream and were informational; do not infer data loss from identity turnover alone.
findings.reopenWhen: Live CSV contradicts the built data, completeness checks fail, a meaningful category disappears, or duplicates demonstrably distort modeled probability.

findings.verification: The agent shell is intentionally read-only with restricted network access. review-input/upstream contains independently fetched public source evidence. Shell DNS failure alone does not establish a public-site outage.
findings.reopenWhen: The trusted collector also fails to fetch the relevant source, or necessary evidence is absent. Name the specific unavailable source and uncertainty.

findings.verification: Official in-game news confirms scheduled December 2 maintenance, accuracy changes, Rock Slide flinch chance, learnset additions, Flash Fire and Stalwart changes. Read current feed/captures; do not apply these future rules before maintenance.
findings.reopenWhen: After effective maintenance, compare updated upstream support and actual app mechanics. Warn if sources or adapters have not adopted live rules.

findings.verification: refresh_meta_usage.py uses HTMLParser for month/table links, including mixed/single/unquoted attributes. tests/test_refresh_safety.py selects the newer pair from the exact mixed-quote reproduction.

Validator compares accepted identities, rejecting missing/same-count replacements. Sharp row loss also rejects partial category mass, while concentrated complete distributions are allowed. Regressions cover all four cases.

Collector now hashes the full body up to 64 MB and saves a compact valid JSON identity summary. The actual source was captured successfully with 347 unique form IDs. It also captures targeted Gogoat/Furfrou/Slurpuff CSV hashes and category counts. A >12 MB regression fixture verifies this behavior.

Export preserves explicit Champions type overrides before Dex mutates its input, producing move-types.js. Browser and calculation workers load the map. Growth is Grass in display/search; Snap Trap is Steel, including engine overrides. Browser regression covers Growth in Abomasnow Grass search.
